note: Values sampled from pixel data. Body colors are the flat face value of each can; highlight/shadow are the render's cylinder gradient stops, useful for recreating the can look in CSS.

ink.role: Primary text/wordmark on light cans (Lime, Pineapple)

cream.role: Primary text/wordmark on dark cans (Cranberry). Also the warm off-white for page backgrounds.

paper.role: Neutral studio background from the render. Good page background.

surface.role: Table/shadow neutral. Borders, dividers, muted UI.

metal.role: Aluminum rim. Use as a 3-stop linear gradient for metallic accents.

flare_white.role: Lens-flare core. Pure highlight / glow center.

usage_rules: Lime and Pineapple are near-white in luminance terms. Never put white or cream text on them — use --sans-ink. Both clear 10:1 with ink.

Cranberry is the only flavor color dark enough for cream/white text. Cream on Cranberry is 5.86:1 (passes AA for normal text, AA-large for headings). White on Cranberry is 7.5:1 if more headroom is needed.
Ink on Cranberry is 2.64:1 and fails. Do not do it.
Do not tint the ink or cream per flavor. The packaging uses one ink and one cream across the line; keeping that constant is what makes the SKUs read as one brand.

The lens-flare motif is the brand's signature graphic device. Reproduce it as a radial gradient from --sans-flare with a faint chromatic ring, plus scattered low-opacity hexagons in the flavor's bokeh colors.
